page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Dalv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AES cryptography, and SHA extensions. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It contains no local storage, though it is premium storage capable, and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU scoring 3079.67 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2077.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4753.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 7558.85. However, memory performance is a notable bottleneck. The PassMark memory score falls in the bottom 10% at 1098.32, and memory bandwidth read-only benchmarks are weak, measuring 303.64 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 36.9 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

Due to its compute-heavy, low-memory profile, the D4als_v6 is suited for workloads that prioritize raw single-core CPU speed over memory capacity or high memory bandwidth. It achieves average results in static web serving and small-model LLM inference, but performs poorly on memory-intensive tasks, database operations, and larger LLM models. This makes it a cost-efficient option for lightweight compute-bound tasks, single-threaded processing, and basic web serving, while being less suitable for large-scale databases or memory-heavy applications.
